story: Senate Commerce advanced S. 5171, the Children's Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026, cosponsored by Alaska's Lisa Murkowski, a bill that orders a federal plan and a study rather than regulating AI toys directly.

claims.claim: The Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation held Executive Session 24 on August 5, 2026 at 10:00 AM.
claims.verbatim: August 5, 2026, 10:00 AM
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation
claims.note: Committee's own meeting notice.

claims.claim: The markup was held in room SR-253, with entry through SR-254.
claims.verbatim: SR-253 (enter through SR-254)
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation

claims.claim: Five bills were listed on the executive session agenda.
claims.verbatim: S. 737, SCREEN Act
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation
claims.note: Count derived by enumerating the legislation section of the published agenda, claims C04 through C08.

claims.claim: S. 737, the SCREEN Act, was the first bill on the agenda.
claims.verbatim: S. 737, SCREEN Act
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation
claims.note: The agenda lists the short title only.

claims.claim: S. 1748, the Kids Online Safety Act, was on the agenda.
claims.verbatim: S. 1748, Kids Online Safety Act
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation

claims.claim: S. 4199, the Youth AI Privacy Act, was on the agenda.
claims.verbatim: S. 4199, Youth AI Privacy Act
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation

claims.claim: S. 4407, the CHATBOT Act, was on the agenda.
claims.verbatim: S. 4407, CHATBOT Act
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation
claims.note: The congress.gov page for S. 4407 returned HTTP 403, so sponsor and full title are unverified. Short title only.

claims.claim: S. 5171 appears on the agenda under the title Children's Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026.
claims.verbatim: S. 5171, Children's Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation

claims.claim: Three of the five bills on the agenda carry artificial intelligence or chatbot subject matter in their titles.
claims.verbatim: S. 4199, Youth AI Privacy Act
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation
claims.note: Derived by counting titles on the verified agenda, S. 4199, S. 4407 and S. 5171. A characterization of titles, not of bill content.

claims.claim: Three Coast Guard nomination items, PN1174, PN1175 and PN1176, were also on the same agenda.
claims.verbatim: James C. Meyers, et. al, dated 07/13/2026, PN1174
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation
claims.note: All three nomination lists are dated 07/13/2026 on the agenda.

claims.claim: The committee's meeting page publishes no vote tally, roll call or recorded result for any bill on the agenda.
claims.verbatim: S. 5171, Children's Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation
claims.note: Verified absence on the fetched page as of the run date. No margin may be stated anywhere in the deck.

claims.claim: Senator Duckworth's office announced on August 5, 2026 that the bill passed through the Senate Commerce Committee.
claims.verbatim: successfully passed through the U.S. Senate Committee on Commerce, Science and Transportation
claims.source_outlet: Office of U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth
claims.note: The committee page carries the agenda but no result, so the outcome is attributed to the sponsor's announcement.

claims.claim: The release is datelined Washington, D.C. and dated August 5, 2026.
claims.verbatim: WASHINGTON, D.C.
claims.source_outlet: Office of U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth

claims.claim: Senator Lisa Murkowski of Alaska is named as the Republican cosponsor of the bill and is the only cosponsor named in the release.
claims.verbatim: Duckworth-Murkowski Bipartisan Bill to Protect Children from Dangers of AI Toys Passes Committee
claims.source_outlet: Office of U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth
claims.note: The congress.gov cosponsor list returned HTTP 403. Say the release names Murkowski, not that she is the sole cosponsor of record.

claims.claim: The bill requires the Federal Trade Commission and the Consumer Product Safety Commission to give Congress a coordinated plan on AI-enabled toy products.
claims.verbatim: provide Congress with a coordinated, actionable plan to address these emerging AI-enabled toy products
claims.source_outlet: Office of U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth
claims.note: The sponsor's description of the bill. The bill text was unreachable, so no deadline or reporting interval may be printed.

claims.claim: The bill directs the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering and Medicine to conduct a study into AI-enabled toys.
claims.verbatim: conduct a comprehensive study into AI-enabled toys examining a wide range of issues
claims.source_outlet: Office of U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth
claims.note: Sponsor's description. No study deadline is stated in the release.

claims.claim: The obligations the sponsor's release describes are a plan and a study, and the release describes no rule, ban or standard on AI toys.
claims.value: plan plus study, no rule described
claims.verbatim: provide Congress with a coordinated, actionable plan to address these emerging AI-enabled toy products
claims.source_outlet: Office of U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth
claims.note: A statement about the RELEASE, not about the bill text, which could not be fetched. Never assert the bill text contains no other provision.

claims.claim: Murkowski said artificial intelligence is rapidly evolving and that a careful understanding of how young people interact with it is needed.
claims.verbatim: Artificial intelligence is rapidly evolving, and we must have a careful understanding of how our young people interact with this groundbreaking technology
claims.source_outlet: Office of U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth
claims.note: Murkowski's own senate.gov press pages returned HTTP 410, so this is not corroborated on her own site.

claims.claim: Murkowski said AI-enabled toys have the potential to significantly impact the development of children.
claims.verbatim: AI-enabled toys have the potential to significantly impact the physical, mental, and emotional development of our children
claims.source_outlet: Office of U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth
claims.note: Print exactly as in verbatim.

claims.claim: Murkowski said she is grateful the Commerce Committee agrees that policymakers and families need this knowledge.
claims.verbatim: It is imperative we equip policymakers and America's families with the knowledge they need to make informed choices about these devices, and I am grateful the Commerce Committee agrees
claims.source_outlet: Office of U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth

claims.claim: Duckworth said AI chatbots were never meant to be used by young children yet are being embedded inside toys by the thousands.
claims.verbatim: These AI chatbots were never meant to be used by young children, yet they're being embedded inside toys by the thousands
claims.source_outlet: Office of U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth
claims.note: The word thousands is the senator's own characterization and carries no cited count. Never render it as a measured figure.

claims.claim: Duckworth said AI-enabled toys have given children information that could put them in immediate danger.
claims.verbatim: We've already seen far too many instances where AI-enabled toys have imparted information to our children that could put them in immediate danger and have long-term impacts on their development
claims.source_outlet: Office of U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth

claims.claim: Duckworth called on the full Senate to pass the bill.
claims.verbatim: now the Senate must pass it with haste, for the sake of our kids' safety
claims.source_outlet: Office of U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth
claims.note: Fragment only. The full sentence on the page joins it with an em dash, which house rules bar.

claims.claim: The release says independent testing by the U.S. PIRG Education Fund in December 2025 found AI toys discussing sexually explicit content and explaining where to find knives, pills and matches in the home.
claims.verbatim: found AI toys discussing sexually explicit content and explaining where to find knives, pills and matches in the home
claims.source_outlet: Office of U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth
claims.note: The underlying PIRG report returned HTTP 403. Attribute on any slide as Senator Duckworth's office citing U.S. PIRG Education Fund testing. Do not state a number of toys tested.

claims.claim: The release states that OpenAI issued an explicit warning that ChatGPT is not meant for children under age 13.
claims.verbatim: Open AI put out an explicit warning that ChatGPT is not meant for children under age 13
claims.source_outlet: Office of U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth
claims.note: Not verified against OpenAI's own policy page. Attribute to the release.

claims.claim: The release names no endorsing organizations for the bill.
claims.verbatim: Duckworth-Murkowski Bipartisan Bill to Protect Children from Dangers of AI Toys Passes Committee
claims.source_outlet: Office of U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth
claims.note: Verified absence across two fetches.

claims.claim: The Consumer Product Safety Commission news release index carried no 2026 release on AI-enabled toys or chatbots in children's products when it was read on August 15, 2026.
claims.verbatim: News Releases
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission
claims.note: Verified absence on the first page of the agency's own release index only. Guidance and recalls live elsewhere on the site.

claims.claim: The Federal Trade Commission press release index carried no current release on AI-enabled toys or companion chatbots and children when it was read on August 15, 2026.
claims.verbatim: Press Releases
claims.source_outlet: U.S. Federal Trade Commission
claims.note: Verified absence on the visible page of the release index on the run date only. The FTC has prior 6(b) activity on AI companions this check does not cover.

claims.claim: The Anchorage Daily News opinion piece on Alaska AI policy was written by Roger Kaye, a freelance writer based in Fairbanks.
claims.verbatim: Roger Kaye is a freelance writer based in Fairbanks
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News
claims.note: Primary as the publisher of the opinion, not as an authority on Alaska law.

claims.claim: The opinion piece carries a published date of August 10, 2026 on the page while its URL path reads 2026 08 09.
claims.verbatim: Published: August 10, 2026
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News
claims.note: Both were checked and they disagree. Cite the on-page date.

claims.claim: The opinion piece states that Alaska House Bill 47 provisions criminalizing AI-generated child sexual abuse material and deepfake harassment passed as part of an omnibus crime bill and became law in June.
claims.verbatim: HB 47's provisions criminalizing AI-generated child sexual abuse material and deepfake harassment passed as part of an omnibus crime bill and became law this June
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News
claims.note: Single sourced to an opinion column. BASIS and LegiScan both returned HTTP 403. Any slide must attribute it and must not print a day.

claims.claim: The opinion piece states that House Concurrent Resolution 3 would have created a task force to study AI in Alaska and recommend how the state should approach its use.
claims.verbatim: HCR 3 would have created a task force to study AI in Alaska and recommend how the state should approach its use in government, education and everyday life
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News
claims.note: Author's characterization. BASIS was unreachable.

claims.claim: The opinion piece says the House Concurrent Resolution 3 effort stalled.
claims.verbatim: That effort stalled, but the need it was meant to address has only grown
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News
claims.note: Write stalled, never died or was voted down.

claims.claim: The opinion piece states that roughly 30 states have passed election-related deepfake disclosure laws ahead of this year's midterms.
claims.verbatim: Roughly 30 states have passed election-related deepfake disclosure laws ahead of this year's midterms
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News
claims.note: Single sourced and uncited in the column. The word roughly is not optional and the attribution is not optional.

claims.claim: The opinion piece states that some states now require companion chatbots to disclose that they are not human or therapists.
claims.verbatim: Some states now require companion chatbots to disclose that they aren't human or therapists, watch for signs of suicidal thinking and block sexual content from reaching minors
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News
claims.note: The column names no state and gives no count. Do not name a state and do not convert some into a number.

claims.claim: The opinion piece makes no mention of Alaska Senate Bill 2.
claims.verbatim: Published: August 10, 2026
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News
claims.note: Recorded so the deck does not inherit an SB 2 reference the scouts attached to this source.

claims.claim: The congress.gov page for S. 5171 returned HTTP 403 to an automated read on August 15, 2026, so the bill text could not be read and no deadline for the plan or the study could be established.
claims.source_outlet: congress.gov
claims.note: Records the read RESULT on the run date, the same way C27 and C28 record an index read. GovTrack also returned 403. This is why no due date appears anywhere in the deck.

claims.claim: The U.S. PIRG Education Fund report behind the testing the sponsor's release cites returned HTTP 403 to an automated read on August 15, 2026, so the testing was verified only as the sponsor's account of it.
claims.source_outlet: U.S. PIRG Education Fund
claims.note: Records the read RESULT on the run date. The number of toys tested and the method remain unknown, so neither may be printed.

killed.claim: Senate Commerce reported out S. 5171 on August 5th with a recorded vote.
killed.why: The committee page publishes the agenda but no tally, roll call or result. The action survives as C12, sourced to the sponsor's release. No margin may be printed.

killed.claim: S. 5171 was introduced on a given date by a given sponsor with a given cosponsor count.
killed.why: congress.gov returned HTTP 403 and GovTrack returned HTTP 403. Only the title and number from the committee agenda survive.

killed.claim: The National Academies study covers risks to children's physical, mental, emotional and social safety and well-being.
killed.why: The four part scope could not be reproduced as a verbatim string on a second pass. The release's broader wording is kept in C16.

killed.claim: Alaska's statute book on AI systems that talk to children is close to empty, or Alaska has zero such statutes.
killed.why: No source was reached that enumerates Alaska statutes on AI or companion chatbot disclosure. BASIS, LegiScan and NCSL all returned HTTP 403. An unverified absence is not a claim. THIS KILLED THE RUN'S FIRST THESIS and the deck was rebuilt around what the record does support.

killed.claim: Alaska House Bill 47 became law on a specific day in June 2026.
killed.why: The opinion column says this June with no date, and the legislative record was unreachable.

killed.claim: The CHATBOT Act is sponsored by a named senator and does X.
killed.why: Only the number and short title are verified, from the agenda.

killed.claim: Murkowski issued her own release on S. 5171.
killed.why: Two Murkowski senate.gov URLs returned HTTP 410 Gone. Her quotes are verified only on Duckworth's site.

killed.claim: Roughly 30 states have election deepfake disclosure laws, stated as established fact.
killed.why: Survives only as C34, an attributed characterization by an opinion author.

killed.claim: Senator Gillibrand is connected to this bill.
killed.why: The release mentions her only in connection with a separate March letter, which was not fetched.

unresolved: The recorded committee vote or voice vote on S. 5171 is not published anywhere reachable this run.
The bill text of S. 5171 is unread, so the deadlines for the FTC and CPSC plan and for the National Academies study are unknown.
The sponsor of record, introduction date and full cosponsor list of S. 5171 are unverified because congress.gov and GovTrack both return HTTP 403.
Whether the other four bills on the agenda were also advanced on August 5th is unknown.
The Alaska Legislature BASIS system returns HTTP 403 to automated fetch, so HB 47, HCR 3 and SB 2 statuses rest on one opinion column.
No source was found that counts Alaska statutes addressing AI systems that interact with children.
The U.S. PIRG Education Fund December 2025 testing report could not be read directly, so the number of toys tested and the testing method are unknown.
Whether the FTC or CPSC has issued any non press release guidance on AI-enabled toys was not checked beyond each agency's release index.
